analysis.title: Louisiana-Pacific Corp. (LPX): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: LPX reported 3Q26 adj. EPS of $0.39 vs GS estimate $0.06 and FactSet consensus $0.20. The beat came from an adj. EBIT margin of 5%, 380bps above GS's model (+$0.27 to EPS), non-operating items (+$0.05) and revenue 4% above GS's flat forecast (+$0.02).
GS says the quarter reflects initiatives to protect OSB margins and expand siding volumes, despite slowing housing activity, weaker consumer confidence and rising inflation in the quarter.

4Q26 guidance is weak. Siding EBITDA guide is $85mn at the midpoint, 5% below GS's model, with a ~22% siding margin vs GS's 23% and siding sales up 3% YOY vs GS +4%. OSB EBITDA is guided to ($35)mn vs GS ($23)mn.
4Q26 consolidated adj. EBITDA guide is $35mn at the midpoint, well below GS at $59mn and consensus at $52mn.

OSB segment: sales rose 1% YOY vs GS -14%, on 7% volume growth and a 6% price decline. Adj. EBITDA margin rose ~153bps YOY to ~(13.6%), 17pts above GS's forecast, largely due to a $14mn lower inventory reserve adjustment.

Siding segment: revenue rose 7% YOY vs GS +5%, with volume up 2% and price up 5%. EBITDA margin fell ~125bps YOY to ~25.2% but was ~56bps above GS's model, as positive price/cost was offset by higher maintenance costs and inventory reduction headwinds. Other items were ($12)mn vs GS ($15)mn.
Balance sheet: net debt/EBITDA of 0.3x, down from 0.4x in 2Q26 and up from 0.1x a year ago, with $265mn cash and ~$1.0bn total liquidity. No shares were repurchased in 3Q.
2026 capex is now expected at ~$300mn, down from ~$320mn, with ~$140mn for strategic initiatives and ~$160mn for maintenance.
GS keeps a Sell rating and a $64 12-month price target, based on 12.0x its Q5-Q8 EBITDA estimate. The stock closed at $75.58 on 2 Nov 2026, implying 15.3% downside.

Questions GS will ask on the call: siding channel inventories and distributor reorganization, siding demand by end-market and price point, siding price vs volume against inflation, siding profitability drivers, OSB capacity and productivity, structural products, inflation and price/cost, and capital allocation and FCF.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 EPS beat on OSB margins, but the 4Q consolidated adj. EBITDA guide of $35mn is well below GS at $59mn and consensus at $52mn. GS keeps its $64 target, 15.3% below the $75.58 price.

earnings_insights: LPX 3Q26 adj. EPS reported $0.39 vs GS estimate $0.06 and FactSet consensus $0.20 (reported 11/3/2026 per the note's date).
3Q26 adj. EBIT margin of 5% was 380bps above GS's model, adding $0.27 to EPS. Non-operating items added $0.05 and revenue 4% above GS's flat forecast added $0.02.
3Q26 OSB sales +1% YOY vs GS estimate -14%, with volume +7% and price -6%. OSB adj. EBITDA margin was ~(13.6%), 17pts above GS's forecast, largely from a $14mn lower inventory reserve adjustment.
3Q26 siding revenue +7% YOY vs GS estimate +5% (volume +2%, price +5%). Siding EBITDA margin was ~25.2%, down ~125bps YOY and ~56bps above GS's model.

4Q26 company guidance: siding EBITDA of $85mn at the midpoint (5% below GS's model), OSB EBITDA of ($35)mn (GS estimate ($23)mn), consolidated adj. EBITDA of $35mn (GS estimate $59mn, consensus $52mn).
GS 4Q26 EPS estimate shown in the table is $0.11 (estimate, pre-guidance). FY26E EPS is $0.95 and FY27E EPS is $1.65.
risk_factors: Upside risks to GS's Sell rating: siding industry demand exceeds expectations, company initiatives drive profitable share gains, effective capital allocation, stronger OSB segment results, and successful new product development.
Slowing housing activity, weaker consumer confidence and rising inflation, which GS cites as the backdrop to the quarter.
Siding channel inventory reductions and the reorganization of distributors.
